jobs.description:
**About FACS**


At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.

**Our Values**


We live our mission through three core values:

* **People First:** Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
* **Integrity of the Science:** Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence\-based practices.
* **Client Relationships for Life:** Build long\-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

**Why Join Us**

* **Impact:** Contribute meaningful work that empowers teams and drives results across the organization.
* **Culture:** Thrive in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission\-driven environment where your work matters.
* **Growth:** Innovate, develop your skills, and help shape the future of how we operate and deliver on our mission.
* **Visibility:** Partner directly with leadership and cross\-functional teams to make a real difference.


Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications—so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.

*Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at* FACS Experts.


**About the Role:**


The Environmental Health Specialist will support public health and well\-being by conducting fieldwork and environmental assessments for a variety of environmental health and industrial hygiene projects. Under the direction of Project Managers, you will support projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.


This is a field\-based role that requires regular travel to local client sites and occasional travel outside the local area, depending on project needs. You will collect samples and field data, document site conditions, prepare accurate field notes, and communicate project updates to Project Managers.


This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys hands\-on work, takes pride in accuracy and professionalism, and is eager to develop technical experience in environmental health and industrial hygiene. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong attention to detail, reliability, a positive work ethic, and a willingness to learn beyond their current comfort zone.

**Responsibilities:**

* Perform assigned fieldwork and project tasks under the direction of Project Managers.
* Travel regularly to local client sites and occasionally to out\-of\-area locations based on project needs.
* Support environmental health and industrial hygiene projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.
* Review project scopes, site requirements, and field protocols to ensure a clear understanding of assigned work.
* Collect field data and samples in accordance with established procedures, project specifications, and safety requirements.
* Conduct site observations and document field conditions accurately and thoroughly.
* Prepare, organize, maintain, and transport the tools, equipment, and supplies needed for assigned fieldwork.
* Maintain detailed field notes; compile data; and summarize findings to support project reporting and analysis.
* Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding project status, technical questions, field conditions, and next steps.
* Report progress, concerns, and deviations from project scope or established protocols promptly.
* Interact professionally and collaboratively with clients, contractors, building occupants, and other stakeholders at project sites.
* Follow all company safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
* Participate actively in training, mentorship, and professional\-development opportunities to build technical knowledge in environmental health and industrial hygiene.
* Support the delivery of high\-quality, timely client service while maintaining FACS’s standards for accuracy, professionalism, and integrity.

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Reliable, professional, and able to follow field protocols, safety requirements, and project instructions.
* Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, current auto insurance, and a driving record that meets company standards.
* Ability to travel regularly to local client sites, with occasional out\-of\-area travel as needed.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of this field\-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on project requirements.

**Preferred**

* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Fieldwork or related experience in environmental services, construction, facilities, EHS, restoration, inspection, sampling, or technical documentation.
* Familiarity with asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, or air and exposure sampling.

**Company Overview:**

**MP Materials (NYSE: MP) is rebuilding American industrial capability for a new era of autonomy, robotics, and electrification.**


We are the only U.S. company with a fully integrated rare earth supply chain—from mining and refining to advanced metal and magnet manufacturing. Our products include both the critical materials used to make permanent magnets and the finished magnets themselves—enabling next\-generation technologies in robotics, automation, aerospace, transportation, defense, and energy systems. These materials are the foundation of physical AI—the convergence of computation, movement, and control.


We hire ambitious, mission\-driven people who want to tackle complex challenges and shape the future of strategic industries. Our culture is rooted in teamwork, resiliency, and integrity, with a deep commitment to operational excellence and national purpose. MP is rapidly evolving from a materials producer into a leading U.S. manufacturer—and our people are driving that transformation.

**Position Overview:**


Under supervision of the Environmental Manager, the Environmental Specialist serves as the technical expert for environmental compliance. The Environmental Specialist is responsible for developing strategic compliance plans and objectives to meet current, developing, and future regulatory requirements with a focus on water permitting, monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping, while supporting continuous improvement in environmental performance across the organization. This position will ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local water quality standards and regulations.

* Prepare, submit, and maintain all required water permits, including California Regional Water Board, County Water Permits, and SWPPP Reports.

* Develop and deliver water compliance training for employees, contractors, and supervisors.
* Track changes in water regulations and communicate potential impacts to management.
* Support company sustainability initiatives related to water balances, water recycling, and freshwater use.
* Identify opportunities to reduce environmental impact and improve compliance performance.

* Develop an understanding of CalOSHA and MSHA regulations as well as MP Materials Health and Safety Practices.
* Respond to chemical spill emergencies by managing the containment, clean up, and disposal of hazardous materials.

* Effectively maintains high level for knowledge and understanding of environmental regulations and how they apply to the facility in the areas of air, water, and solid waste management.
* Develops and provides necessary training of site personnel so that all facility employees have the knowledge and skills to comply with and enforce environmental regulations and policies. Training should emphasize Environmental over Production \- prevention, individual responsibility, and commitment.
**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in environmental or environmental related discipline is preferred.
* 4\+ years’ experience in environmental or environmental related fields.

**Desired Qualities:**

* Professional certifications not required but are a plus: CEP, QEP, and/or CES.
* CA State Water Boards D1 Operator certification is preferred; or be able to acquire certification within 6 months of hire date.
* Excellent verbal, interpersonal, and written communication skills.
* Ability to effectively train and direct others (peers, employees, contractors/vendors).
* Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
* Knowledge of industrial plant processes and equipment.
* Knowledge of industrial plant operations and maintenance requirements.
* Project management skills.
* Employee relations skills and ability to motivate others.
* Knowledge of regulatory and corrective action tracking programs.

**GFT** is seeking a **Project Environmental Scientist** to join our growing Environmental Practice! This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring regular attendance at either our **Berkeley, CA or Roseville, CA** offices.  

GFT’s Environmental team delivers integrated planning, permitting, and compliance solutions that support infrastructure development across North America. With more than 140 professionals in 22 offices, the team guides clients through NEPA and permitting processes, ecological and regulatory assessments, and environmental remediation efforts. Their expertise spans transportation, power, water, and facilities markets — working alongside agencies at federal, state, and local levels. From stream restoration to complex regulatory requirements and advance critical infrastructure projects. **What you’ll be challenged to do:**
This is an excellent career opportunity for an experienced, motivated Project Environmental Scientist who is ready to take the next step in their career. We are looking for someone how combines strong technical permitting expertise – a professional that enjoys doing the work, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies and helping to building a growing environmental practice.
The successful candidate will have strong working knowledge of California and federal environmental permitting requirements, particularly as they apply to transportation, water and power projects. * Prepare and manage permit applications and supporting technical documentation, including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, and other applicable federal, state, and local permits and approvals.

* Conduct wetland delineations, jurisdictional assessments, biological field studies, and other technical investigations necessary to support project permitting as well as CEQA/NEPA analysis.
* Author and review technical reports, CEQA/NEPA analysis, permit applications, environmental commitments, mitigation plans, and related environmental deliverables.
* Work closely with engineering and design teams to identify natural resource and permitting constraints, develop practical avoidance and minimization measures, and incorporate environmental requirements into project design and construction.
* Support environmental compliance during construction, including implementation and tracking of permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
* Manage environmental permitting assignments, including scope, schedule, budget, staffing, deliverables, and client communications.
* Contribute to and increasingly lead environmental components of proposals, interviews, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
* Contribute to the continued development of GFT’s California Environmental Practice.

* Strong working knowledge of applicable federal and California environmental regulations.
* Experience working with and developing relationships with regulatory agencies such as USACE, CDFW, RWQCB, USFWA and/or NOAA Fisheries.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Self\-starter, able to complete tasks with minimal supervision and direction.
* Willingness to travel and execute work in a variety of settings and environmental conditions (heat, cold, rain, etc.).
* Demonstrated leadership and interpersonal skills to work effectively with others and achieve results.
* Demonstrated agility working with multi\-disciplined infrastructure projects.

* Ability to prepare and deliver presentations and lead meetings, when needed.

**What we prefer you bring:*** A Master’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology or a closely related field.
* Established relationships with California transportation agencies, water agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, or other infrastructure clients.

jobs.description:
**Description**
---------------


The Bay Area Air Quality Management District (Air District) is a regional government agency, committed to achieving clean air to protect the public's health and the environment. The Air District accomplishes this goal through regulation of industrial facilities and various outreach and incentive programs designed to encourage clean air choices.
  

  

The Air District's jurisdiction encompasses all of seven counties \- Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara and Napa, and portions of two others \- southwestern Solano and southern Sonoma.
  

  

The Air District is currently accepting applications for the position of Senior Air Quality Specialist in the Regulatory Development Division. This is an open recruitment for one (1\) full\-time, represented position.


**About the Position**


The Senior Air Quality Specialist will serve as lead in reviewing and drafting regulatory language for various air quality rule programs; work closely with professional and technical staff to interpret complex scientific research and economic and environmental analyses and technical work for developing regulations to control air pollutants (including those contributing to climate change and contributing to localize air quality impacts in overburdened communities).


Develop and implement cost effectiveness and incremental cost effectiveness calculations for a wide variety of sources in industry with a variety of control options; analyze emissions inventories to determine baseline emissions and reduction estimates for rules under development; brief District executives and present at workshops, committee and board meetings; work closely with the Community Engagement Section staff and other Air District divisions to strengthen partnerships with key community stakeholders; perform related work as assigned.


The Regulatory Development Division works with all levels of the Air District, including staff, management, executives, and Board members in developing and modifying Air District rules to provide emissions reductions to improve air quality both regionally and at the neighborhood level and protect the climate. Apex Companies is seeking a dynamic and experienced Senior Technical Project Manager (PM) to join our growing team in Pleasant Hill, CA. This key leadership position will drive the successful delivery of complex environmental investigation, remediation, and compliance projects involving soil, groundwater, sediment, soil vapor, surface water, and other environmental media. The role requires strong technical leadership, exceptional client management skills, and a proven ability to mentor staff, manage project execution, and support business growth. Experience with industrial, manufacturing, petroleum, government, and brownfield remediation programs is highly desirable.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
**Project and Program Management**


* Manage large\-scale environmental investigation, remediation, and compliance projects from proposal through closure.
* Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, work plans, and health and safety plans.
* Lead multidisciplinary teams of geologists, engineers, hydrogeologists, risk assessors, and environmental scientists.
* Monitor project financial performance, including revenue, profitability, utilization, and forecasting.
* Coordinate subcontractors, laboratories, drilling contractors, and remediation vendors.
* Maintain quality assurance and quality control standards.


**Technical Leadership**


* Serve as a technical lead for sites impacted by a range of chemical and petroleum\-related contaminants in soil, groundwater, sediment, soil vapor, surface water, and other environmental media.
* Design and oversee:
	+ Site investigations and environmental assessments
	+ Soil and groundwater characterization
	+ Soil vapor and vapor intrusion assessments
	+ Human health and ecological risk assessments
	+ Remedial investigations/feasibility studies (RI/FS)
	+ Corrective action and site closure programs
* Evaluate and implement appropriate remediation approaches and technologies based on site conditions, regulatory requirements, and project objectives.
* Interpret environmental data, evaluate remedial alternatives, and develop practical recommendations for investigation, remediation, and long\-term site management.


**Client Relationship Management**


* Act as primary client contact for key accounts.
* Support strategic planning with industrial, manufacturing, petroleum, commercial, and government clients.
* Prepare and present technical findings to clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
* Maintain long\-term client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.


**Business Development**


* Lead proposal preparation and pricing.
* Support capture planning and opportunity pursuit.
* Identify new clients and expand existing accounts.
* Participate in industry organizations and conferences.


**Regulatory Expertise**



Demonstrated experience working with:


* EPA CERCLA/Superfund programs
* RCRA Corrective Action
* State cleanup and voluntary remediation programs
* Vapor intrusion guidance
* UST and industrial facility closure programs
* Applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations


**Qualifications**


* BS in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Hydrogeology, Geology, or related field.
* 12\+ years of environmental consulting experience.
* 7\+ years managing complex environmental investigation and remediation projects.
* Demonstrated success managing projects exceeding $500K to $5M\+ annually.
* Significant experience with environmental investigation, remediation, and regulatory compliance involving contaminated soil, groundwater, and other environmental media.
* Professional certifications such as PE, PG, CHG, PMP, REM, or CHMM preferred.


**Why you'll love working for us:**


* Company\-subsidized medical and dental.
* Company\-paid life, short, and long\-term disability.
* 401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
* Cross\-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
* Performance\-based bonuses or other incentives.
* Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
* 2,000\+ employee national firm with 70\+ locations across the US.

Each task gives you a user request and the answers three different models gave to it. * Support strategic planning with industrial, manufacturing, petroleum, commercial, and government clients.
* Prepare and present technical findings to clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
* Maintain long\-term client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.

* Support capture planning and opportunity pursuit.
* Identify new clients and expand existing accounts.
* Participate in industry organizations and conferences.


**Regulatory Expertise**



Demonstrated experience working with:


* EPA CERCLA/Superfund programs
* RCRA Corrective Action
* State cleanup and voluntary remediation programs
* Vapor intrusion guidance
* UST and industrial facility closure programs
* Applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations


**Qualifications**


* BS in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Hydrogeology, Geology, or related field.
* 12\+ years of environmental consulting experience.
* 7\+ years managing complex environmental investigation and remediation projects.
* Demonstrated success managing projects exceeding $500K to $5M\+ annually.
* Significant experience with environmental investigation, remediation, and regulatory compliance involving contaminated soil, groundwater, and other environmental media.
* Professional certifications such as PE, PG, CHG, PMP, REM, or CHMM preferred.

* Company\-subsidized medical and dental.
* Company\-paid life, short, and long\-term disability.
* 401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
* Cross\-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
* Performance\-based bonuses or other incentives.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Cap\-and\-Invest Program has a position available for a motivated Air Pollution Specialist (APS) with knowledge of forestry practices to conduct a variety of activities related to development, implementation, and analysis of the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol. This work supports the California Air Resources Board’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions programs, principally the Compliance Offset Program within the Cap\-and\-Invest Program. The available APS position is in the Program Operation Section, which is situated in the Climate Change Program Evaluation Branch of the Industrial Strategies Division.  

Under direction of an Air Resources Supervisor I, the incumbent will participate as a member of high\-level technical (engineering and scientific) teams established to address technical and policy issues associated with the development of protocols and projects for the reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions as part of California's Cap\-and\-Invest Program.  

The duties for this position are primarily focused on implementing the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol. The incumbent will assess U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol projects, including forest inventory methods, and assist offset project operators with compliance and verification matters. The incumbent will develop technical and statistical tools and approaches for assessing forest carbon quantification, monitoring, and reporting applicable to the Compliance Offset Program and other forest\-related and land conservation efforts. The incumbent will take actions to address issues and questions related to the implementation of the U.S. Forest Protocol and the Cap\-and\-Invest Regulation and develop guidance to support implementation of the Compliance Offset Program. The incumbent will also be responsible for assisting with the development of updates to the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol and the associated provisions in the Cap\-and\-Invest Regulation and for supporting rulemaking processes to adopt new compliance offset protocols.
The incumbent will develop a variety of reports, briefing papers, guidance documents, speeches, and presentations to communicate about the Compliance Offset Program, and will work with management to evaluate proposals and recommend creative solutions to climate change challenges. The incumbent may also be called upon to serve as a lead person for workgroups, technical meetings, and audits of verification bodies and projects, and to engage in events with industry, environmental groups, government organizations, and the public. The incumbent may assist with review of offset project types other than forest projects.

Synopsis:
At the City of Melville, we're committed to creating a safe, healthy and sustainable environment for our residents. We're looking for motivated Environmental Health Officer to join our dedicated team and play a vital role in protecting public health through education, compliance and proactive environmental health initiatives.


Working within our Environmental Health team, you'll undertake a diverse range of regulatory, advisory and educational activities while partnering with residents, businesses and internal stakeholders to deliver high\-quality environmental health outcomes.


If you enjoy working collaboratively, solving complex problems and engaging with the community, we'd love to hear from you.

  

**Location:** City of Melville Civic Centre


**Salary:** $83,200\.00 to $111,296\.64 pro\-rata p.a. \+ 12% Super


**Employment Type:** Permanent, Full Time

  

**What You’ll Be Doing**


* Conducting inspections, assessments and investigations across a variety of environmental health matters
* Assessing development applications and processing environmental health applications
* Delivering proactive environmental health programs, sampling and compliance activities
* Providing professional advice to residents, businesses and internal stakeholders
* Supporting enforcement activities, including investigations and legal proceedings where required
* Mentoring the Environmental Health Assistant and contributing to continuous improvement across the team
* Assisting the Senior Environmental Health Officer in delivering efficient and effective environmental health services
  

**What We’re Looking For**


* A current ‘C’ Class Driver's Licence
* Qualifications recognised for appointment as an Environmental Health Officer in Western Australia
* Eligibility for appointment as an Authorised Person and Inspector under relevant legislation
* Demonstrated experience in environmental health inspections, investigations and compliance activities
* Sound knowledge of relevant environmental health legislation, including the Food Act 2008, Health (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1911 and Environmental Protection Act 1986
* Strong communication, negotiation and report writing skills
* The ability to manage competing priorities while delivering high\-quality customer service

Local Government experience, food safety auditing knowledge and previous mentoring experience will be highly regarded.

  

**How to Apply**


Apply online via the Apply button and provide a comprehensive resume and cover letter (no more than 2 pages) demonstrating fulfilment of essential requirements outlined in the Position Description attached.


**Closing Date: Sunday, 04 Oct 2026, 11\.59PM AWST.**


For further information about this position, please contact: **Chiat Chew, A/ Manager Health and Compliance on 08 9364 0281\.**


If you are interested in this exciting opportunity, we strongly advise you apply as soon as possible as the City reserves the right to close this advertisement before the closing date.

  

**Why The City of Melville?**


We are a welcoming and diverse community that enjoys a blend of retail and business precincts and an abundance of open spaces in a unique, natural landscape, along the shores of the beautiful Swan and Canning Rivers.


We are proud to be recognised as an Inclusive Employer 2024\-2025 – a prestigious award that benchmarks workplace inclusion across various diversity areas. This recognition is the only one of its kind in Australia and highlights our commitment to fostering a workplace where diversity is celebrated, and inclusion thrives. In everything we do, we focus on our EPIC values of Excellence, Participation, Integrity and Caring and we aim to achieve an inclusive, vibrant, and sustainable future.

  

**Why Belong?**


Elevate your work experience with the City of Melville’s benefits!


* Enjoy annual salary increases of 4%, effective each year from 1 July 2025 to 1 July 2027
* Enjoy flexible working arrangements that help balance work and life
* Stay active with a free LeisureFit membership
* Save time and money with free on\-site parking
* Celebrate your special day with Birthday Leave – no work on your big day!
* Access paid parental leave to support your family
* Take more time to recharge with 2 extra days of leave plus the option to purchase additional leave (up to 10 weeks off per year)\*
* Benefit from a generous superannuation co\-contribution of up to 15\.5%
* Maximise your pay with salary packaging and novated leasing options
* Grow your career with structured professional development and study assistance programs
* Look after your wellbeing with wellness initiatives and Employee Assistance Programs
* Connect outside of work with a vibrant social club
* conditions apply


The City of Melville celebrates diversity, inclusion, and belonging. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including but not limited to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally diverse backgrounds, and people living with disabilities.


All candidates applying for a position where the use of ‘plant and machinery’ or driving a vehicle is an inherent requirement of the role and other ‘high risk’ facilities where public safety is at risk, will be required to pass a drug and alcohol test as part of a pre\-employment medical.


We appreciate the interest from Recruitment Agencies in collaborating with us, however, at this time, the City of Melville is managing the recruitment process for this role. Please refrain from submitting candidate profiles to our team. Rest assured, should the need for external assistance arise in the future, we will not hesitate to reach out to recruitment agencies.
